title: Legal Research Assistant Optimization
business: Corporate legal departments managing high volumes of internal policy queries.
problem: General-purpose LLMs often lack the specialized domain knowledge required to accurately interpret complex legal terminology, leading to inconsistent or hallucinated responses.
solution: Implementing the law-chat model, which utilizes continued pre-training on domain-specific corpora to enrich the LLM with legal knowledge while maintaining conversational capabilities through reading comprehension techniques.
steps: Initialize the environment using the transformers library to load the law-chat model.
Define a system prompt that aligns with the LLaMA-2-Chat structure to ensure safe and coherent responses.
Format user inputs as multi-turn conversations to fit the model's expected input structure.
Execute inference using the model to generate responses based on the provided legal context.
outcome: Improved accuracy in handling domain-specific legal queries compared to standard general-purpose models.
limitation: Continued pre-training can sometimes degrade the model's general prompting ability; verify performance by testing against baseline general-purpose tasks.

diagram.description: The flow of data from user input to the specialized legal response.

code.content:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('AdaptLLM/law-chat') # Load model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('AdaptLLM/law-chat') # Load tokenizer
prompt = '<s>[INST] <<SYS>>\nYou are a helpful assistant.\n<</SYS>>\n\nQuestion: Define ex post facto. [/INST]'
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors='pt').input_ids # Tokenize input
outputs = model.generate(inputs, max_length=512) # Generate legal response
